source_identity.display_name: SimCLR histology encoder + random forest (HEST; Ciga et al.)
source_identity.identity: SimCLR histology encoder of Ciga et al.
source_identity.configuration: Frozen patch embeddings scored by HEST with its 70-tree random-forest regression head.
source_identity.basis: HEST §5.2 lists 'Ciga Ciga et al. [2022] (SimCLR pretrained on public histology data)' among its ten patch encoders, and Table 1 scores their embeddings with a 70-tree random forest. The cited paper applies SimCLR to 57 unlabelled histopathology datasets. The printed label 'Ciga' is the first author's surname, so the display name describes the method and keeps the attribution.
source_identity.source_locator: HEST arXiv:2406.16192v1 §5.2, p.6; Table 1, p.7; App. C.3, pp.14 and 17; Table A12, p.26. Ciga et al. arXiv:2011.13971v2 abstract, p.1. github.com/ozanciga/self-supervised-histopathology README at f7a93798911c861efa297fd9c9b9b1f9ece0c1c0; github.com/martellab-sri/self-supervised-histopathology README at 22d3440f8d94d6e367304f1e50b82e9ea930dbd7.

known_details.value: Random forest with 70 trees (sklearn) mapping patch embeddings to log1p-normalised expression of the top 50 highly variable genes, scored by Pearson correlation.

known_details.label: Pretraining

known_details.source_locator: HEST §5.2, p.6; Ciga et al. abstract, p.1

records.description: Base method introduced by Karimi et al. (2019). Evaluated configurations, retrained weights and their scores are separate records.

entity_classification.rationale: The cited paper names DeepAffinity as a learned compound-protein affinity predictor. This record covers the method family described there; no checkpoint or variant is implied.
entity_classification.source_locator: arXiv:1806.07537v2 title and abstract, p.1; §§2.4-2.5, p.4
ambiguities: The paper reports separate and unified RNN-CNN models, three attention mechanisms and a graph (GCNN) variant. Configurations must state which variant they used.

profile.summary: DeepAffinity predicts compound-protein affinity from a compound SMILES string and a structure property-annotated protein sequence (SPS), using pretrained recurrent seq2seq encoders followed by convolutional layers.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GRU seq2seq auto-encoders are first trained without labels on compound SMILES and protein SPS strings. In the unified RNN-CNN model, a 1D convolution and max-pooling layer is added after each encoder, the two outputs are concatenated and passed through two fully connected layers, and the whole pipeline is trained end to end with the pretrained encoders as initialisation. A separate RNN-CNN baseline keeps the encoders fixed.

sections.title: Protein representation
sections.body: In the original paper, SPS strings group residues into secondary structure elements using secondary structure and solvent accessibility predicted from sequence by SSpro/ACCpro.

sections.title: Variants
sections.body: The paper also describes separate, marginalized and joint attention mechanisms trained jointly with the encoders and CNN, and a unified RNN/GCNN-CNN variant that replaces the compound RNN with a graph CNN.
sections.source_locator: arXiv:1806.07537v2 §2.5, p.4 and PDF p.8; README Table of contents

profile.summary: DeepDTA predicts drug-target binding affinity from a ligand SMILES string and a protein sequence, using a separate 1D convolutional encoder for each.
profile.summary_source_locator: arXiv:1801.10193v2 abstract, p.1; Proposed model and Figure 2, PDF pp.7-8

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: SMILES strings and protein sequences are label-encoded characters. Each passes through its own block of three 1D convolutional layers, where the second and third layers have two and three times the filters of the first, followed by max-pooling. The two pooled vectors are concatenated and fed into fully connected layers of 1,024, 1,024 and 512 units, with dropout after the first two, and a regression output trained with mean squared error.

sections.title: Original evaluation
sections.body: The paper evaluates on the Davis kinase dataset (Kd) and the KIBA dataset. It fixes maximum lengths of 85 SMILES and 1,200 protein characters for Davis and 100 and 1,000 for KIBA.
